security_audit.summary: Most system-reconnaissance and command-execution alerts are false positives caused by license text, Markdown backticks, and design prose. The remaining confirmed issue is the low-severity binary-font blind spot, with added semantic findings for unrestricted font downloads and user-context spoofing.

remediation.issue: Fictitious prior user instruction in SKILL.md
remediation.suggestion: Remove the claim that the user already requested perfection. Rephrase it as an optional refinement guideline.
Use bundled, vetted fonts by default. Require explicit approval before downloading external assets.

remediation.issue: Bundled binary font assets need provenance
remediation.suggestion: Publish source URLs and hashes for each .ttf file, or replace binaries with reviewed package references.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md claims the user already requested a pristine masterpiece. This fabricates user context and can pressure the model to follow a non-user instruction.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The line directly asserts a prior user request that may not exist. It does not request secrets, so confidence is high but not certain malicious.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted External Asset Acquisition
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs agents to download whatever fonts are needed. This can trigger unreviewed network access and importing untrusted binary font files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction explicitly allows open-ended font downloads. Legitimate design use is possible, but unrestricted downloads create a clear supply-chain risk.

content.value_statement: Static visual design often needs clear art direction before production. This skill creates a visual philosophy and guides polished PNG or PDF canvas artwork.
actual_capabilities: Creates a concise visual philosophy before producing final artwork.
Guides poster, art print, and static design composition for PNG or PDF output.
Emphasizes typography, spacing, color, form, and visual hierarchy.
Uses bundled font files from the canvas-fonts directory when appropriate.
Supports single-page output and multi-page visual series when requested.
limitations: It provides design instructions, not a standalone rendering engine.
Final quality depends on the host AI tool and available file-generation tools.
External font downloads require review in controlled environments.
It is focused on static artwork, not interactive interfaces or animation.

use_cases.title: Produce Campaign Posters
use_cases.description: Create a visual direction and final static artwork for events, announcements, or cultural campaigns.

use_cases.title: Develop Editorial Art
use_cases.description: Turn an article theme, book concept, or magazine feature into a visual-first PNG or PDF composition.

use_cases.title: Explore Brand Directions
use_cases.description: Generate an aesthetic direction with typography, color, and spatial rules for early identity exploration.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Poster
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one static design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a one-page poster for a community workshop about sustainable repair. Use minimal text and export a PNG.

prompt_templates.title: Build Editorial Artwork
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with a clear subject and tone.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a design philosophy and one PDF artwork for an essay about quiet technology in public spaces.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Identity Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a visual philosophy for a small architecture studio, then create a refined static canvas showing the direction.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Multi-Page Series
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three related pages for a coffee-table art series about memory, maps, and urban night light. Keep text sparse.

output_examples.input: Poster for an experimental jazz night with a restrained but intense mood.
output_examples.output: A short design philosophy, then a one-page PNG poster with sparse typography, structured marks, and a limited palette.

output_examples.input: Editorial artwork for an article about climate data and personal memory.
output_examples.output: A PDF artwork using layered grids, subtle reference markers, and small labels to express the subject visually.

output_examples.input: Visual direction for a ceramic studio launch.
output_examples.output: A quiet brand-art composition with paper-like texture, careful spacing, and minimal text integrated into the canvas.

best_practices: Give the subject, audience, output format, and required text before generation starts.
Provide brand colors, dimensions, and accessibility needs when they matter.
Review the design philosophy before final output when accuracy is more important than speed.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for text-heavy documents that need detailed reading flow.
Do not request imitation of living artists or copyrighted visual styles.
Do not allow unrestricted external asset downloads in controlled environments.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a design philosophy and uses it to guide static PNG or PDF visual artwork.

faq.question: Does it create interactive designs?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on static canvas artwork, posters, and PDF pages.

faq.question: Can it use custom fonts?
faq.answer: It can reference bundled fonts, but external font downloads should be restricted or reviewed.

faq.question: Can it make multiple pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide a related multi-page visual series when the user requests it.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What input should users provide?
faq.answer: Users should provide the subject, audience, mood, output format, and any required text.
